_comment: Ten EU and UK institutional feeds. Tier 1 sources get a small scoring bonus over tier 2. Scope is deliberately EU + UK only. EUR-Lex was removed on 24 Aug 2026: it returns 403 to GitHub's runners. The European Parliament feed is retained but returns empty to them for the same reason. 'verified' means the endpoint parses; it says nothing about whether the feed is still being updated — read the Age column in the digest's health table for that.

sources.name: Council of the EU — external relations documents
sources.note: Replaces EUR-Lex, which refuses GitHub's servers. Primary Council documents - decisions, regulations, conclusions - in the external relations file, which is where sanctions law lives. Titles arrive as document codes, so the parser swaps in the descriptive subject line.

sources.name: Council of the EU — press releases
sources.note: Where sanctions packages are actually adopted. Carries some French-language items; the noise list drops them.

sources.name: European Commission — press corner
sources.note: Checked 26 Aug 2026: parses, but newest item was 31 Jul — four weeks stale. The staleness column in the health table will now say so on every run.

sources.name: European Parliament — press releases
sources.note: Committee stages, votes and trilogue outcomes - the in-progress pipeline. BROKEN as of 26 Aug 2026: returns an empty body on every run ("no element found: line 1, column 0"). The top-stories feed is worse — dead since 2023. Needs a replacement from https://www.europarl.europa.eu/at-your-service/en/stay-informed/rss-feeds ; until then the health table shows the failure on every run rather than hiding it.

sources.name: OFSI — financial sanctions (HM Treasury)
sources.note: General licences, designations, enforcement. The single best UK sanctions source.

sources.name: FCDO — sanctions and foreign policy
sources.note: UK designations and the Sanctions List updates.

sources.name: Department for Business and Trade
sources.note: Export controls, trade remedies, and UKCA/CE marking - the divergence beat's UK end.

sources.name: gov.uk — news and communications
sources.note: Broad catch-all across departments. High volume, so the filter does the work.

sources.name: DEFRA — food, farming and biosecurity
sources.note: SPS checks and the border target operating model - the sharpest edge of EU-UK divergence. Same gov.uk pattern as the other four, but unconfirmed; check the health table.

sources.name: UK Sanctions List — designations and changes
sources.note: Designations, licences and enforcement notices across departments. The first attempt pointed at a publication page's .atom, which 404s — gov.uk only serves feeds from organisation and search paths. This uses the same search endpoint as govuk-news, narrowed by keyword; the local filter still does the real work, and in-run dedupe handles any overlap. Confirm in the next health table.

sources.name: DSIT — science, innovation and technology
sources.note: Added 26 Aug 2026, confirmed live (newest item 24 Aug). Carries the cyber and digital file, which is a divergence story before it is a tech story — the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill is the current example.
